content.en: The **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** was signed in 1947 by 23 nations. Its primary objective was to facilitate **trade liberalization** by reducing **tariffs** and other trade barriers. It operated on the principle of **Most-Favored-Nation (MFN)** treatment, which ensures that trade concessions granted to one member are extended to all other members.

definition.en: Ensuring equal treatment among trading partners through MFN status.

content.en: GATT functioned through periodic negotiation rounds aimed at lowering tariffs globally.

content.en: Students often confuse GATT as a formal international organization; it was actually a multilateral treaty.
